applicant_utility.summary: This is a professor-led grant, not a personal scholarship: a tenured associate or full professor at a Finnish university applies as Principal Investigator for their own ICT project and uses the EUR 75,000 to hire a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher. The 2026 window ran 18 May to 15 September 2026 and decisions are scheduled for late October 2026, with funded work starting early 2027 and ending by August 2028. Watch the site from spring 2027 for the next annual call, and note that a successful project can reapply for an extension through that round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Tenured associate and full professors at Finnish universities leading a genuinely new, high-risk ICT direction who need salary funding to recruit a researcher.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the project plan early: there is no template and no length cap, so plan a structure that makes innovativeness obvious within the first pages
Build the budget line by line before writing the narrative, since the salary, overhead and other-expense split must add up to 75,000 EUR exactly
Write the ethics and research-security section deliberately rather than as a token paragraph; the Foundation asks for it to be comprehensive
Identify the intended hire and include their CV if possible, since including an already-identified researcher is explicitly called beneficial
Create your grant-system login well before September, since work on the portal only begins after registration
common_rejection_risks: Proposals that read as incremental extensions of existing work rather than something with genuinely new frontiers
A financial plan that does not disaggregate salary, overheads and other expenses into a credible total
A thin or generic ethics and research-security discussion
Submitting a second application in the same call when only one per professor is allowed
Treating the grant as money for the professor's own time rather than for a hired researcher
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the hired researcher's salary, overheads and the project's other expenses: the grant is a fixed 75,000 EUR pot, so any cost overrun, equipment, travel or additional personnel must come from other funding.
document_audit: The project plan has no official template, so evaluators compare unstructured proposals against each other; a clearly labelled structure with headings for aims, method, novelty, risk and plan is safer
The financial breakdown must reconcile with the 75,000 EUR total and should be defensible against real Finnish university salary and overhead rates
If a researcher is already identified, their information must be included rather than left as a promise to recruit later
alerts: The 2026 call closed on 15 September 2026; the page for the current round is closed, so do not plan around an immediate submission
Decisions are scheduled for late October 2026 and projects may only begin in early 2027, so hiring cannot start before the award
The project must conclude no later than August 2028, which constrains how you schedule a doctoral recruitment
One application per professor per call means the project you choose is the only bet you can place that year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Nokia Foundation grant system, complete the online form as PI, attach the project plan and financial plan in the free-format allowed, and submit before the 23.59 cut-off on deadline day.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a personal mobility grant for postdocs and assistant-professor-level tenure-track scholars at Finnish universities: the money pays the costs of a research visit abroad, explicitly not your salary. The standard ceiling is 30,000 EUR for a 12-month visit, rising to 50,000 EUR only with exceptional justification such as travelling with family, and shorter visits are scaled down proportionally. Both 2026 windows have closed (17 April and 15 September), so plan for the next twice-yearly round. Grants are awarded one year at a time for a maximum of three years, with renewals applied for during the ongoing award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs and assistant professors at Finnish universities in ICT, data science/AI, wireless networking or microelectronics who already have a credible host abroad and need visit funding rather than salary.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the host professor's invitation letter first; without it the application is incomplete regardless of the research plan
Frame the visit as a single host organisation for one year, since that is the Foundation's explicit recommendation
Map your topic explicitly onto one of the three focus areas (Data Science and AI, Wireless and Network Technologies, Future Microelectronics) rather than assuming ICT is enough
Argue the Finnish benefit line separately: the published criteria include supporting and promoting education and research within Finland
Budget realistically for travel, accommodation and visit costs, and keep salary out of the plan entirely
If renewing, assemble the progress report evidence (articles, manuscripts, conference attendance, posters) before the window opens
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that does not clearly touch one of the three named focus areas
A budget that leans on salary support, which the page rules out
A vague or multi-host visit plan instead of one host organisation for one year
No Finnish benefit argument, despite it being a stated condition
For second and third year applicants, a missing or thin progress report on the earlier grant
Applying while awaiting permission to defend without enclosing the pre-examiners' statements
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The grant covers visit costs only. Your salary, home-institution overheads, any dependants' costs beyond the exceptional ceiling and any relocation not tied to the visit stay on you or your employer.
document_audit: The invitation letter must come from the academic host of the visit and be inside the application, not promised later
Renewal applicants need a progress report that covers research progress, completed articles, manuscripts in progress, conference attendance, posters and presentations
Applicants with official permission to defend must enclose pre-examiners' statements, and the visit can only start after the doctoral degree is completed, so sequencing matters
A family-travel claim for the higher 50,000 EUR band needs its own written justification; it is not automatic
alerts: Both 2026 deadlines have passed (17 April for the Tutkijat maailmalle call and 15 September for the autumn call), so there is no live window at this verification date

Applications can be submitted twice a year, but the two calls are not interchangeable: the spring call runs inside the Tutkijat maailmalle programme while the autumn call runs through the Foundation's own grant system
Awards are one year at a time; a three-year plan needs three successful rounds, and funds are only available for one year after the funding decision
A one-year deferral for personal reasons is allowed only if the project plan stays the same; anything longer goes to the Board case by case
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Nokia Foundation grant system, wait for the relevant call to open, then submit the plan, budget and host invitation letter online; drafts can be saved and finished later.
